action: Position the probe to visualize the bony landmarks. Locate the patella on the right side of the screen.
interpretation: Identify the patella and observe the deep acoustic shadow cast beneath the bony structure.

action: Maintain probe position proximal to the patella. Focus on the soft tissue structures superior to the bone.
interpretation: Visualize the quadriceps tendon, identified by its characteristic horizontal striations.
Extend the field of view to visualize the contour of the femur bone at the bottom of the screen.

action: Fan the probe through the suprapatellar area.
interpretation: Scan specifically for the presence of anechoic fluid to rule out pathology.

action: Survey the suprapatellar recess (the potential space between the tendon and femur).
interpretation: Confirm the absence of knee effusion (transcribed as 'neofusion') in this potential space.

action: Identify the anechoic area currently visible within the tendon structure.
interpretation: Recognize this finding as anisotropy, an artifact caused by ultrasound waves hitting the tendon at a non-perpendicular angle.

action: Rock the probe (heel-toe maneuver) to orient the beam perpendicular to the tendon fibers.
interpretation: Observe the disappearance of the hypoechoic/anechoic area as the angle of insonation is corrected.
Note that this anisotropic artifact is a normal property of tendons, nerves, and similar linear structures.

action: Apply the rocking maneuver whenever a hypoechoic area is visualized within a tendon.
interpretation: Verify perpendicular alignment to distinguish between true pathology and anisotropy.
